modelResponse.episodeSummary: 58-year-old male with ischemic cardiomyopathy presenting with regular wide-complex tachycardia (RVT) and stable hemodynamics.
keyECGEvidence: morphology: Wide monomorphic QRS, RBBB-like morphology with monophasic R in V1
modelResponse.mechanism: Re-entrant ventricular tachycardia facilitated by a scarred myocardial substrate from a prior anterior MI and reduced ejection fraction (LVEF 35%).
contributingFactors: Prior anterior MI (2020, PCI to LAD)

rejectedAlternatives.why: QRS duration of 156ms and monomorphic wide-complex morphology in a patient with known structural heart disease and low LVEF strongly favor VT until proven otherwise.

recommendedActions: Immediate 12-lead ECG and continuous cardiac monitoring.
Assess for hemodynamic stability (BP, pulse, mental status) and oxygenation.
Consult Cardiology for management of symptomatic VT.
Consider synchronized cardioversion if patient becomes hemodynamically unstable.
Maintain current fluid status and monitor for further deterioration.
uncertainty: AV dissociation was noted in the morphology description but not clearly visualized in the provided summary data.
Troponin T 0.04 ng/mL is 'mild HIGH (demand)', but lacks specific trend data to rule out acute coronary syndrome.
